one_month_reasoning: Q3 2026 earnings are expected around 2026-11-02 (not yet confirmed), so they probably fall just outside the window ending 2026-10-29. The main scheduled event inside the window is the 2026-10-28 FOMC. Kalshi and Polymarket price about 44% for a 25bp hike and 55% for a hold (DeFiRate, 2026-09-30; volume not shown). A hike would add to the pressure on a high-beta semi that already fell 9% on the day of the September hike and analyst day, but hike odds fell 21 points this week, so the outcome is close to a coin flip. There may also be early Synaptics deal filings or proxy news, which I expect to have little effect. Short-horizon signals conflict: the stock rebounded about 14% from its 2026-09-16 low of $65.80 after the analyst day, while the 3-month trend is sharply down. The CFO's $8.2M sale leans slightly negative. With no clear edge, I use a symmetric lognormal centred on $76 with sigma of about 0.17, near annual realized vol / 3.5.

fair_value.method: A 60/40 blend of forward P/E (NTM EPS at Sep-2027 of about $4.90 x 16.5x = $81) and FCF yield (about $4.30 FCF/share x 18x, a 5.5% yield, = $78), giving about $80 per share 12 months out.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS as of Sep-2027 (weighted 25% CY27, 75% CY28, pro forma for Synaptics) about $4.90 x 16.5x

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus of $4.53 cut about 7% for Chinese SiC price pressure (wafers about $400 vs $1,200 Western cost) and the auto/China exposure. That puts it near the Q3 guide run-rate ($0.87 midpoint x 4 = $3.48) plus growth.
The Substack base case of $5.72 pro forma (standalone consensus about $6.02), cut about 10% for integration and PPA drag and because management puts margin gains mostly in 2028-30.

Low end of the 16-18x 'cyclical auto/industrial' range in the Substack framework. Discounted because the NTM EV/EBITDA is already only about 12x and the Fed is hiking (prediction markets put about 74% on a December hike).

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM FCF about $1.7B / 395M shares = about $4.30 per share x 18x (5.5% yield)

inputs_detail.derivation: Q2 run-rate of about $1.7B a year, held flat because capex and SiC restructuring offset growth. Consistent with the analyst-day plan to more than double FCF by 2030, since most of that growth is back-end loaded.
The 13.45% Synaptics share issuance is assumed roughly FCF-neutral per share because management targets accretion within 18 months (sources 4, 12).
Between the current depressed NTM EV/EBITDA of about 12x (TIKR) and the 18-22x P/E range in the Substack scenarios. It sits below TI's 18.5x EV/EBITDA to reflect cyclicality.

bear.story: Auto and China demand stays weak and the Chinese SiC price war squeezes margins. The Fed keeps hiking. 2027 EPS comes in around $3.50 and Synaptics integration drags, so the stock rerates to about 13.5x and retests the 52-week low of $44.56.

base.story: Gross margin moves into the low 40s as utilization rises and fab divestitures proceed. AI data center revenue doubles to about $1B in 2027 and the Synaptics deal closes mid-2027 without surprises. EPS runs at about $4.9 NTM x 16.5x.

bull.story: The AI power ramp plus an auto and industrial recovery push EPS toward the high end of the 2027 range (about $5.40), with visible progress toward the 2030 targets ($11B revenue, 53% gross margin). The multiple returns to about 22x, taking the stock back toward the pre-deal level of about $115-120.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $52 the stock would trade at under 11x consensus 2027 EPS, about 20% under the April lows before the AI data center rerating. That level would most likely mean a real earnings reset: gross margin guided back below 38%, AI data center revenue failing to double in 2027, a SiC impairment, or a bad Synaptics integration or dilution surprise. Ordinary volatility is unlikely to explain it.

reasoning: ON has round-tripped from $58 in March 2026 to $134.92 in June (AI power rerating), then fell to $66 by mid-September. The drivers were the all-stock Synaptics deal (1.35 ON shares per SYNA share, about 13.45% dilution, stock -20-25%), a sell-the-news Q2 print, and the 2026-09-16 analyst day, which put most margin gains in 2028-30 (2030 targets: $11B revenue, 53% gross margin). A Fed hike landed the same day. Fundamentals are actually improving: Q2 revenue +9% YoY, non-GAAP gross margin 39.3%, FCF $425M, and the Q3 guide is for a 40-42% gross margin and $0.87 EPS. Consensus 2027 EPS is $4.53 and the street target is about $104. Alternative and lane sources add several points. TrendForce and Evertiq both report Czech SiC job cuts, with onsemi calling in-house wafers uneconomic against Chinese $400 wafers, which cuts both ways: lower cost but a price war. Workopia shows about 466 open postings, mostly fab and operations, with no sign of a hiring freeze. Prediction markets price more Fed hikes, a macro headwind for the multiple. Insider flow is only selling (CFO $8.2M). The independent Substack puts pro forma CY28 EPS at about $5.72 and values the stock at $82-139, with a base of $104. I haircut consensus and use a 16.5x P/E and an 18x FCF multiple, which gives a fair value of about $80, slightly above spot. The scenarios are bear $48 / base $82 / bull $120 at 25/50/25 (mean about $83). The ladder is a lognormal with median about $80 and sigma about 0.48, below the 64% realized vol, because that realized figure is inflated by the one-off deal gap but still well above a typical large-cap. Research limits: X/Twitter was not searched directly, the Castellano Substack was paywalled, and the prediction-market volume was not visible.
